Abdul Malek, Senior Advocate instructed by Shamsul Haque Siddique, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioner.

full_judgment:
Mustafa Kamal J: Accused-petitioner Khandoker Saiful Islam along with two others were convicted under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and sentenced to imprisonment for life and to pay a fine of Taka 10,000.00 each in default to suffer RI for 2 years more each. Another accused Abdus Samad was convicted under section 323 of the Penal Code and sentenced to suffer RI for 1 month more by the learned Sessions Judge, Gaibandha by his judgment and order dated 18-7-88 in Sessions Case No.4 of 1988. On appeal, Criminal Appeal No. 651 of 1989 a Division Bench of the High Court Division by judgment and order dated 20-8-96 altered the conviction of the accused-petitioner and two others to part 1/34 of section 302 of the Penal Code and reduced the sentence to rigorous imprisonment for 10 years each, upholding the conviction and sentence passed against accused Abdus Samad. 

 3. Shortly stated, the prosecution case is that on 31-5-87 at about 7-00 AM the informant PW 1 Badsha Miah along with deceased Kadem Ali, his brother PW 12 Saheb Miah and others went to cut jute plants in the decretal land of PW 1 being plot No.3771 to the south-west of his house. At this time the accused-petitioner Khandoker Saifullslam, Chairman of the local Union Parishad, along with the other accused persons being armed with falas. lathis, daggers, axes, etc. came and attacked the informant and his companions. Petitioner Khandoker Saiful Islam caught hold of Kadem Ali who accompated PW 1 and gave an order to kill him when convicted accused Lal Miah dealt a blow with a holonga on the chest of Kadem Ali. Petitioner Khandoker Saiful Islam then released the victim who fell down on the ground whereupon convicted accused Ismail Hossain dealt a blow with a dagger on the left side of the cliest of KademAIi.PWI4 Foyez Ali came to the rescue of KademAli when he was assaulted on the head by accused Abdus Samad with a lathi causing serious injury on his head and PW 14 fell down unconscious on the ground. Kadem Ali succumbed to his injuries on the spot, PW 1 lodged the First Information Report at 11-30 AM on the same day and the police after investigation submitted charge-sheet against 18 accused persons. The prosecution examined 19 witnesses and tendered one as against 3 witnesses by the defence on a charge under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and on a separate charge under section 325 of the Penal Code against accused Abdus Samad. 

 4. The defence case is that, the original owner of plot No. 3771 was Abed Pradhan who died leaving behind 5, sons and 2 daughters. The informant and his brother claimed inheritance through the two daughters of Abed Pradhan. They had no possession in the disputed land. They obtained an ex parte decree in a partition suit against which a miscellaneous case under Order IX rule 13 CPC is pending. They took delivery of possession through Court only on 28-5-87, ie only three days before the occurrence. The jute plants were not grown by the informant party but by the accused party who had both title and possession of the disputed land. The informant party, after obtaining symbolical possession through Court, went to the disputed land to protest criminal trespass and mischief to the crops by the informant party and in the process a free fight took place between the parties and both sides received injuries. The defence raised the plea of the right of private defence of property and person. The counter case filed against the informant party seven days after the occurrence resulted -in the acquittal of the accused informant party. 

 5. The special defence of the petitioner Khandoker Saiful Islam is that he was neither the owner nor the possessor of the disputed land. He mediated between the parties at 6-00 AM on the date of occurrence and left for another place to attend another meeting and was not present at the place of occurrence at all. It was also his defence that the PWs and the informant were inimically disposed towards him as his opponent in the election for the Chairman of the Union Parishad instigated them to file the false case against him. 

 7. Mr Abdul Malek, learned Counsel for the petitioner, now raises the general defence taken by all the accused persons in respect of right of private defence. He submits that the High Court Division has accepted that the informant party went to cut jute plants in the disputed land and there is no evidence that the jute plants were grown by them. They only obtained symbolical possession of the disputed land three days before the-occurrence. The High Court Division accepted that the accused persons in resisting the trespass and mischief to their crops caused injury to the victim. But the High Court Division, taking the view that the informant party was unarmed, that deceased Kadem Ali was in malkocha fashion and that one accused Miaz Ali received injuries which were not grievous enough to justify the apprehension of death to Maiz Ali or any other accused person, the accused persons. exceeded their right of private defence of persons and property and therefore they are guilty of culpable homicide not amounting to murder falling under section 304 part 1 of the Penal Code. Mr Abdul Malek submits that when it is the prosecution case itself that the informant party went to cut jute plants they must have in their hands sickles and therefore the finding that they were unarmed is without any foundation, secondly, the fact that deceased Kadem Ali was found in malkocha fashion obviously means that he was in a fighting mood and not in a defensive position and therefore there were reasonable apprehension of an assault from him. Thirdly, he submits that the fact that accused Maiz Ali did not receive injuries of a grievous nature does not justify the conclusion that there was no apprehension of death or grievous hurt from the informant party. 'The' fact that accused Maiz Ali received injuries is good enough reason to justify the apprehension of death or grievous hurt. 

 8. The right of private defence is dealt with under secLions96-1 06 of the Penal Code. Even if the special defence of alibi and electoral rivalry is left out of consideration, the accused-petitioner under section 96 of the Penal Code can invoke his right of private defence in defence of the immovable property of any other person; the disputed land not being his: but under section 100 of the Penal Code the right of private defence of the body extends to the voluntary causing of death if the offence which occasions the exercise of the right is an 'assault which may reasonably cause the apprehension of either death or grievous hurt The evidence in the case must be such that the informant party was carrying on or was about to carry on an assault of such nature.
